dataset_size.description: Number of examples/items in the benchmark, as an integer; null if not stated. Count the full evaluation set, not a single subset or split

primary_evaluation_setting.description: How models are primarily evaluated. Use EXACTLY one of these four lowercase values and nothing else: zero-shot, few-shot, fine-tuned, mix. Use 'mix' whenever more than one setting is used (including zero-shot plus few-shot, or zero-shot plus chain-of-thought). Do not add qualifiers, articles or explanations

gold_source.description: How the reference answers (ground truth) were produced. EXACTLY one lowercase value: existing_metadata (lifted from a documentary process that already described the object — catalogue records, library or museum metadata, archival finding aids, structured databases), authored_answer_key (lifted from pre-existing material authored as assessment or reference: exam and quiz answer keys, textbook solutions, standardized tests, encyclopedia entries), crowd_annotation (annotators without disciplinary training, hired or recruited for this benchmark), domain_expert (annotators with training in the relevant humanities discipline), paper_authors (the authors wrote the items and answers themselves), model_generated (an LLM or other model produced, translated or filtered the reference answers), not_stated (the paper does not say). The distinction between existing_metadata and authored_answer_key matters: a curatorial record and a GRE answer key carry different kinds of authority. If the benchmark mixes sources, report the one covering the majority of items and describe the mix in facets_explanation

gold_beyond_stimulus.description: Does answering correctly require knowledge NOT present in the stimulus given to the model (image, passage, document)? EXACTLY one of: yes, no, not_stated. Judge the reference answer, not the difficulty: identifying a figure from a caption already in the input is 'no'; identifying it from iconographic attributes that must be matched against an external tradition is 'yes'

gold_community_dependent.description: Does the benchmark treat the correct answer as varying by cultural or linguistic community? EXACTLY one of: yes, no, not_stated. 'yes' requires positive evidence — per-region or per-language gold answers, locale-specific splits, or explicitly community-relative correctness. A benchmark that is merely multilingual while keeping one universal answer key is 'no'

gold_concerns_genesis.description: Is the target of the task a property of how the artefact came to be — date, author, place of origin, provenance, material history — rather than a property of its content? EXACTLY one of: yes, no, not_stated. Report 'yes' only if such items form a substantial part of the benchmark, not if one minor subtask happens to include dating

answer_multiplicity.description: How many answers does the scoring accept per item? EXACTLY one of: single_answer (one key, exact match or one correct option), answer_set (several enumerated answers accepted), graded_human_judgment (scored by human or LLM judges on a scale rather than matched against a key), not_stated

plurality_treatment.description: How does the paper treat divergence between annotators, or between defensible readings of the same material? EXACTLY one of: noise (disagreement is filtered out, resolved by majority vote, or reported as low inter-annotator agreement to be minimized), signal (disagreement is preserved and treated as informative about the material itself), not_stated (the paper does not discuss it). Report the paper's stated stance, not your own view

facets_explanation.description: 2-4 sentences giving the evidence in the paper for the facet values above, especially where sources are mixed or the paper is ambiguous. Paraphrase the paper's own description of how the dataset and its reference answers were built

reported_format_gap.description: Does the paper report, for the SAME models on the SAME material, a performance difference between two answer formats or two difficulty regimes? EXACTLY one of: yes, no, not_stated. Qualifying comparisons: multiple-choice vs open-ended/generative on the same items; exact match vs partial/per-field match; a standard split vs a 'hard' or adversarial split of the same benchmark; with-image vs text-only versions of the same questions; a shallow vs a deep tier of the same taxonomy (e.g. surface description vs interpretation layers). NOT qualifying: one model beating another, one language beating another, a metric changing across different benchmarks, or an ablation of the model rather than of the task format. Report 'no' when the paper evaluates a single format throughout and says nothing of the kind; 'not_stated' only when the paper reports no numeric results at all

reported_format_gap_points.description: The LARGEST such gap the paper reports, in percentage points, as a positive integer (e.g. multiple-choice 94% falling to 23.9% on open completion is 70). If the paper reports the comparison on a 0-1 scale, convert to points (0.658 vs 0.04 is 62). If the paper gives a range, take the upper bound. null when reported_format_gap is not 'yes' or when no number is given

human_baseline_reported.description: Does the paper report a quantified human baseline, human expert score, or human inter-annotator agreement ceiling that model scores are compared against? EXACTLY one of: yes, no. A vague mention of human evaluation without a number is 'no'

human_gap_points.description: Percentage points between the best reported model and the human baseline, as an integer: human minus best model. Positive when humans lead (human 92.4, best model 61.4 is 31); negative when the best model exceeds the human baseline. null if human_baseline_reported is 'no' or the two are not on the same metric

reported_best_score.description: The headline score of the best-performing model on the benchmark's primary metric, as a number on the paper's own scale (e.g. 13.4 for 13.4% accuracy, 61.1 for an F1 of 61.1). null if the paper reports no single headline figure

reported_best_metric.description: The name of the metric reported_best_score is measured on, lowercase and unqualified: accuracy, f1, exact_match, bleu, cer, wer, pass@1, win_rate, cosine_similarity, human_score, other. null if reported_best_score is null. Scores on different metrics are not comparable — this field exists so aggregation can restrict itself to one metric at a time

reported_cultural_asymmetry.description: Does the paper report a SYSTEMATIC performance difference across cultures, languages, regions or traditions — not merely that it evaluated several? EXACTLY one of: yes, no, not_stated. 'yes' requires the paper to state the asymmetry as a finding (e.g. Western-centric bias, degradation on low-resource languages, worse scores on a named region). 'no' when the paper covers multiple cultures or languages and reports no such difference. 'not_stated' when the benchmark is monocultural or monolingual and the question does not arise

results_explanation.description: 2-4 sentences giving the evidence for the results fields above, QUOTING the paper's own figures verbatim (model names, numbers, metric names, split names) so every value can be checked against the paper. Where a number was converted or derived (a 0-1 scale turned into points, a range reduced to its upper bound), say so explicitly. If a field is null, say in one clause why the paper gives no such figure
